messages:
maria: sharing a quick writeup of the new bench methodology we ran today. high level: compare synthetic load (poisson + burst) vs replay harness for kernel selection and batching heuristics. results in the doc + raw traces attached.
ashok: awesome — did you keep the same seq_len distribution across both? that's usually the tricky bit for KV cache behavior
maria: yes, we sampled seq_len from prod traces and forced the same distribution into the synthetic generator. also added a 10% long-tail spike (>=1024) to stress kernel switching.
jin: nice. what about sampler for prompt prefixes? synthetic often misses warm KV warmup patterns
maria: good call — synthetic runs include a prefix affinity model: 60% cache-friendly prefixes, 30% cold-start, 10% repeated sequences to exercise KV reuse. we log KV hit ratio per shard.
sophie: pinging the bench-bot to upload perf profiles
bench-bot: uploaded artifacts to s3://redwood-bench/1797009876/ (profiles, traces, config.json)
kevin: can you paste the kernel selection trace? curious when we fallback to int8-kernel vs fp16
maria: pasted snippet:
```
# selection log (shortened)
step 1: choose fp16_kernel (seq<=512, batch<=8, latency_slo=120ms)
step 2: at t=360s spikes -> choose spec_kernel_int8 (quantized) due to throughput
step 3: long seq -> use tiled_attention_kernel (memory safe)
```
ashok: interesting — tiled_attention jumps latency a lot for p50 but saves OOMs for p95
maria: exactly. p50 improved with speculative decoding enabled for int8, but p95 regressed by ~18% in latency due to tiled attention path.
jin: did you try KV caching warmup window tuning? smaller window might avoid tiled path for repeated short queries
maria: yes, we tested kv_ttl={30s,120s,600s}. 120s seemed like sweet spot: KV hit + batching increase without moving many requests to tiled path.
kevin: what about apples-to-apples with quant profiles? sometimes int8 vs q4h tradeoffs differ by model family
maria: we created matched latency buckets and compared quality with the same decode seeds + evaluation prompt set. q4h had slightly better qual (BLEU/ROUGE proxies) but cost ~12% higher.
sophie: any perf regressions flagged automatically?
bench-bot: regression_gate: p95_latency increased by 18% vs baseline; quality delta vs baseline: -0.6% (within tolerance). Regression ticket created: INF-4821
maria: logged INF-4821 with perf traces and kernel decision heatmap. action items: 1) try speculative decoding threshold adjustments, 2) re-evaluate quant profile (q4h fallback), 3) profile tiled_attention hot loops for optimization
ashok: i'd add: run a focused microbenchmark for tiled_attention with varying batch shapes. may reveal kernel selection heuristics need a different cost model
jin: agreed. i can prepare a replay harness that replays only long-tail sequences with KV warmup to reproduce the p95 hit
kevin: also test allowing dynamic fallback: prefer fp16 for p95-critical customers by policy override. that might be a quick mitigation.
maria: noted. i'll update the bench config and re-run overnight. leaving the trace labels so we can diff later.
ops-bot: deploy-check: bench harness will run on staging-gpu-2, estimated runtime 6h. notify channel on completion.
sophie: thanks, team. small reminder to include decode seeds for exact apples-to-apples quality comparators :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — will post results and a short TL;DR tomorrow.
